summary: Collett Cox is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda and also studied in Japan. She served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999, 2017).

Conor Roddy works in philosophy and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) under Kathleen Marie Higgins, having also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) was a scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin, he held posts at the universities of Leipzig (~1856–1861), Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934). He subsequently held a post at Columbia University from around 1952 to 1980.

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a BA from Smith College and a PhD from Emory University (attested 2014) supervised by John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining the Smith College faculty (attested 2014).
Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University by 2012.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was a linguist, Indologist, and Tibetologist. Educated at Paris and the University of Warsaw, he taught at Warsaw (1936), Fribourg (1945), and the University of Lausanne (1945, 1949–1957).

Corneille Jest (1930–2019) was a Tibetology and archaeology scholar. He studied at Paris Descartes University, studied under André Leroi-Gourhan in 1972, and held a post at the CNRS from around 1956 to 1995.
Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under the supervision of Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a religious studies scholar. Educated in Amsterdam, he became a professor at the Remonstrant Seminary in 1873 and held the chair in history of religions at Leiden University from 1877 to 1901.
Corrado Pensa is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as a professor at the University of Rome (attested 1971).
Craig J. Reynolds is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Australian National University, attested in 1996 and 2016.

Craig Jamieson is an Indology and Buddhist studies specialist. He held posts at the University of Cambridge, serving as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012), and was a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2012).
Craig Preston is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins from 1980 to 1981.

Cristina Pecchia specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Rome (~1999–2003) and also studied at Vienna. Around 2007, she held posts at the University of Vienna and the IKGA.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied under figures including Emmanuel Levinas, and held professorships at the University of Lausanne (~1998–2012) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2000–2015).

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an Indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1997) and a PhD at Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2003, he became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She has held posts as an assistant professor of Buddhist studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa (1944–2021) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
